origins: When career, children at home, or health-related roles change, the schedule and the sense of mission change too. Without clear tasks, days feel empty and the question “What am I for?” arises.
teaches: “The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me” (Psalm 138:8). “He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.” Jesus said, “Love the Lord your God… and love your neighbor as yourself.” Those two purposes do not retire. Paul says we are God’s workmanship “created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance as our way of life.” Purpose is not only a job title. It is loving God and others in whatever season.
self_statements: I have no reason to get up.
I have nothing to live for.
errors: Believing purpose is either a career or nothing.
Predicting that I will always feel empty.
Feeling aimless and concluding that I have no purpose.
questions: What roles have I lost, and what have I gained?
What are the two great commands, and how can I live them today?
Who is near me who could use a kind word, a meal, or a prayer?
What skills or interests have I set aside?
What did I love as a child or young adult?
What is one thing to do this week that matters to someone?
truth: My purpose is bigger than a job or role. God’s purposes for me continue, and I can love Him and my neighbor in this season. He will complete what He began in me.
hw_truths: The Lord will fulfill His purpose for me.
He will complete His work in me.
I was made for good works.
I can love God and neighbor.
God is not finished with me.
log: Each week, note one act of love for God or neighbor.
actions: Write the old and new ones.
Ask God to show your purpose.
prayer: Lord, You will fulfill Your purpose for me. Show me how to love You and my neighbor in this season, and use me today. Amen.
